info.title: Permguard Host API
info.description: The Host listener (WP-2.5): `/host/v1` over TLS on `admin.addr`, and `permguard.host.v1` on the same port, one facade behind both. Every route authorizes with the Host's grants; every mutation carries a request id, may state the revision it expects, and answers a receipt. Identity, membership, evidence and the key and configuration mutations arrive with their packages; this document describes what this build serves.

post.description: Under `identity.admin` on the Host (WP-4.1). Each coordinator asked to revoke the memberships this Host is a member of; the memberships it coordinates ended here; the identity retired, its public evidence kept under `host/identity/retired/`, its private keys destroyed and a new identity provisioned. The process signs nothing more and serves the new identity after a restart.

get.summary: One page of the verification bundle
get.description: Under `keys.read` on `resource` (WP-3.4). The identity, every public key the rings published, every ring binding issued and the revocations, and, for a resource an active membership's task covers, each member this Host coordinates (its manifest, its identity and the ring statements the manifest pins, listed by a `peers` item the frontier's digest names; WP-4.1), at a frontier the first page fixes. The first page signs the manifest once, COSE_Sign1 `permguard.keys.bundle.v1` under the `host.operations` key active at the frontier; later pages present it as `frontier` and receive the same bytes, so a rotation in between changes nothing. The items of all pages together are the ones the manifest counts and digests. Never private material.

parameters.description:
The resource the bundle covers, in the Host API's grammar: `host`, `plane/

`, `plane/

/zone/`, `plane/

/zone//ledger/`.

parameters.name: frontier
parameters.description: The manifest a first page answered, base64url, which the Host checks it signed; absent on the first page, which fixes the frontier.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Where the page starts, as the page before answered it; requires `frontier`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many items the page carries: 1 to 500, 100 when absent.

token.description: The invitation's token, base64url without padding: proven on the session, never sent and never kept.

requested.description: What this Host asks for, inside the invitation.

request_id.description: The caller's name for this mutation; validated; a sync converges, so a retry fetches again.

SyncMembershipBody.x-grpc-note: `membership_id` travels in the path on REST.

request_id.description: The caller's name for this mutation; a retry is answered with the same plan.

mode.description: `normal`: refused until every coordinator acknowledged its revocation; `emergency`: the memberships no coordinator acknowledged marked `orphaned` and their coordinators named.

reason.description: Why, printable: kept in the audit.

address.description: Where the coordinator is, when this Host is the member; `null` otherwise.

step.description: What the reset does to it: asked of the coordinator, or revoked or rejected here.

ResetMembership.description: One live membership, and what a reset does to it.

plan_digest.description: The plan's digest, SHA-256 hex; the run step presents it back.

expires.description: When the plan can no longer be run, RFC 3339: ten minutes after it was made.

revision.description: The identity epoch the plan was made at; the run is a `conflict` when it or a membership moved.

mode.description: The mode the plan was made in.

IdentityResetPlan.description: What an identity reset plan answers.

request_id.description: The caller's name for this mutation; a retry answers what the run answered.

plan_id.description: The plan the plan step answered.

manifest.description: Its last manifest, COSE_Sign1 `permguard.membership.manifest.v1`, base64url: a coordinator's revocation receipt, or the manifest this Host issued.

coordinator.description: The coordinator that must revoke it out of band.

ResetOrphaned.description: A membership the reset left `orphaned`: terminal here, active for its coordinator until revoked out of band.

host_id.description: The Host it is from the next start.

fingerprint.description: The new identity's first fingerprint: what peers pin.

witness.description: The new identity's external witness: the value of `host.identity.witness` where it is pinned.

restart_required.description: Always `true`: this process signs nothing more and serves the new identity after a restart.

by.description: The declared profile, the approving principal or the verifier id.

AssuranceClaim.description: One claim of an assurance binding, without the record it cites.

current.description: Whether it admits tasks now: accepted, unexpired and, on the coordinator, under the appraisal policy in force.

policy_revision.description: The appraisal policy it was appraised under, `sha256:` and 64 hex digits.

task_ids.description: The tasks requiring controls it covers.

claims.description: One per required control, sorted by name.

appraised_by.description: The principal that approved or appraised it.

expires_at.description: When it stops admitting tasks, RFC 3339.

binding_digest.description: What a task admission answers it by, `sha256:` and 64 hex digits.

AssuranceBinding.description: The assurance binding a membership manifest signs (WP-4.2): the coordinator's appraisal of the controls the tasks require. The records behind the claims, an operator's reason, and evidence are never answered.

control.description: A registered control a task requires.

wants.description: The least class the appraisal policy wants; `null` when it does not appraise the control, which makes the task unapprovable.

declared.description: Whether the member's declared profile meets it.

AssuranceRequirement.description: One control the tasks require, as the policy and the declaration stand.

policy_revision.description: The appraisal policy in force, `sha256:` and 64 hex digits.

nonce.description: The nonce evidence for this revision binds to, 32 bytes base64url: it changes with every revision.

AppraisalState.description: The appraisal state of a membership whose tasks require controls, while the coordinator can appraise it (pending or active).

reason.description: Why, printable, 1 to 512 bytes: kept in the audit, never in the manifest.

expires_at.description: When the approval lapses, RFC 3339, in the future.

OperatorApproval.description: An operator's approval of one control: an accountable risk decision, not attestation. The principal is the caller's.

verifier.description: The id of a verifier registered on this Host.

evidence.description: The evidence, base64url, at most 64 KiB decoded, bound to the appraisal state's nonce; kept by its digest alone.

AttestationEvidence.description: One piece of attestation evidence for a registered verifier.

approvals.description: The operator's approvals, one per control at most. Optional; absent is none.

evidence.description: The evidence, at most 4 pieces. Optional; absent is none.

AssuranceOffer.description: What an approval brings for the controls the tasks require (WP-4.2).

RevokeBinding.description: Why an assurance binding is revoked.

request_id.description: The caller's name for this mutation; a retry answers the stored receipt and manifest.

expected_revision.description: The membership revision the caller read; another is a `conflict` carrying the current.

approvals.description: The operator's approvals. Optional; absent is none.

evidence.description: The evidence, at most 4 pieces. Optional; absent is none.

revoke.description: Revokes the binding instead: it admits no task from then on. Optional; `null` renews it.

AppraiseMemberBody.x-grpc-note: `membership_id` travels in the path on REST.

receipt.description: The receipt; its revision is the membership's.

MemberAppraised.description: What an appraisal answers: the successor manifest with the binding renewed or revoked, still active, a new epoch.
